title: The DVR purity step for a punctured finite etale cover
statement: Let A be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let q:L→Spec A [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] be smooth with geometrically connected fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let V be the open complement of the closed point. Let n:N→L be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale on q⁻¹V [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose W is an open of L containing a point x of the special fibre and n is etale on W. Then there are a finite etale morphism p:E→L and an isomorphism N|q⁻¹V ≅ E|q⁻¹V commuting with the maps to q⁻¹V. Neither normality of E nor density of its puncture is part of this statement. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on q is required.

source.place: Tag 0EYE (Lemma 58.31.3); Tag 0EYJ (Lemma 58.31.8), first two paragraphs of the proof

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer of the DVR A. Smoothness gives flatness, so its pullback defines the special fibre D as an effective Cartier divisor. The DVR is Noetherian; smoothness is locally of finite type, hence L is locally Noetherian. D is smooth over the residue field, so it is regular. This is the geometric setup in the first paragraph of Tag 0EYJ.

The special fibre is geometrically connected and contains x, so it is connected and nonempty. A regular locally Noetherian scheme has disjoint open irreducible components: on each normal Noetherian affine chart the finitely many minimal-prime components cannot meet because the local rings are domains. Connectedness leaves one component, so D is integral. W meets D and hence contains its generic point. The finite etale model n on W extends the punctured cover near that point and witnesses absence of ramification there. This is the only codimension-one point of L on D, because D is an integral effective Cartier divisor. Thus the punctured cover is unramified over L in codimension one, as in the second paragraph of Tag 0EYJ.

Apply Tag 0EYE to L, its regular effective Cartier divisor D, and the finite etale cover n restricted to q⁻¹V=L\D. It gives a finite etale p:E→L with the required restriction isomorphism. Orient that isomorphism from the restriction of N to that of E. The isomorphism is over the open, which gives the displayed composition equality. The theorem asserts existence; no definition chooses an arbitrary witness. The empty cover is included by Tag 0EYE.

theorem exists_finite_etale_extension_of_dvr_neighbourhood
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    {L N : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [Smooth q] [GeometricallyConnected q]
    (V : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hV : ∀ t : Spec (.of A), t ∈ V ↔ t ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    (n : N ⟶ L) [IsFinite n]
    (het : Etale (n ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)))
    (W : L.Opens) (x : L) (hx : x ∈ W)
    (hqx : q x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) (hW : Etale (n ∣_ W)) :
    ∃ (E : Scheme.{u}) (p : E ⟶ L), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧
      ∃ e : (n ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)).toScheme ≅ (p ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)).toScheme,
        e.hom ≫ (p ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)) = n ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)
